max_colors.description: At most this many colours (2-64). With a palette, they are picked from it. On the three tools that have a standard mode — create_character, create_topdown_tileset, animate_object — ANY palette setting needs mode='pro': standard refuses palette and max_colors, alone or together. Every other tool taking them has no standard mode and accepts them always.

palette.description: Target palette, 2 to 256 hex colours as a JSON array, e.g. ["#081820", "#346856", "#88c070", "#e0f8d0"] for Game Boy or ["#000000", "#ffffff"] for 1-bit. Every pixel the tool draws is one of them; pixels you supplied (a direction you drew) stay as they are.

palette_name.description: Optional name of the palette (e.g. 'Game Boy', 'PICO-8'); naming it helps the look. It only LABELS the colours you pass in palette rather than looking any up, so it cannot be sent on its own.

style_image.description: Style anchor. Exactly ONE of its three sources: `url` also accepts an `upload:<id>` from get_upload_url or a data: URL, and `source_image_id` is an image you own (what a Pro Flash job returns). It must fit INSIDE the output canvas both ways — a larger one is refused, so crop it; resizing pixel art is never the answer. Reuse one anchor across calls to keep a set consistent.

usage_description.description: How this reference should guide appearance.

style_options.description: Choose which visual traits to copy from the style image.

width.description: Defaults to 64 for text creation. Native sizes: 16x16 (experimental), 24x24, 32x32, 32x48, 48x48, 64x64, 96x64, 96x96, 128x128. Custom size (Beta): integer width 16–256 and height 16–256. Both dimensions must be multiples of 4 pixels. Pixel-grid recovery uses image-to-pixel-art with fixer when needed. No native image resizing.
